Definition: of Chaldee origin (compare H1355); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem:-- Gabbatha.
BiblicalUsage: Gabbatha is the Hebrew name for the Pavement, the place of Pilate's judgment seat in John 19:13. When Pilate heard the Jews' words, he brought Jesus forth and sat down in the judgment seat, in a place called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha. The name means a raised place, a knoll, and it is the last public spot where Jesus stood before the cross.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the name of the place matters because the judgment seat of a Roman governor became the stage of the world's greatest injustice — and its greatest mercy. Pilate sat down to judge Jesus, and I hold that the Judge of all the earth was standing before him.
